payout_quote: There is a small stipend paid to individual poll workers approximately six weeks after an election. It ranges from about $50 to $150, depending on role and shift worked (half- or full-day). An additional $20 is paid to those who attend training.
steps: Complete the San Luis Obispo County Precinct Worker Application (special applications for student poll workers and Adopt-A-Poll participants).
Attend training before Election Day (required for anyone serving as an inspector; an extra $20 is paid to training attendees).
Arrive at 6:00 A.M. on Election Day to set up.
Work a half- or full-day shift through poll close; close the polls, account for and pack up ballots and supplies, and deliver voted ballots and supplies to a central collection point.
Stipend is paid approximately six weeks after the election.
catches: The stipend is a small amount and paid only about six weeks after the election.
Stipend varies by role and by whether a half- or full-day shift is worked; the county only publishes an approximate $50–$150 range.
The larger $600-per-precinct figures on the county's site belong to the Adopt-A-Poll program paid to organizations, not to individual precinct workers.
biggest_catch: Small, delayed stipend: approximately $50–$150 for a long Election Day, paid about six weeks later.
eligibility: Must be at least 18 years old, a U.S. citizen, and a registered voter in California or a lawful permanent resident of the United States.
timing: Election Day: arrive 6:00 A.M. for setup; polls 7:00 A.M.–8:00 P.M.; then close the polls, account for and pack supplies, and deliver voted ballots and supplies to a central collection point.
weasel_words: approximately six weeks after an election

c1.evidence: San Luis Obispo County's official precinct-worker page: 'a small stipend paid to individual poll workers approximately six weeks after an election. It ranges from about $50 to $150, depending on role and shift worked (half- or full-day). An additional $20 is paid to those who attend training.'

c2.evidence: San Luis Obispo County's official precinct-worker page: 'Election Day, arrive at 6:00 am to set up... Close the polls... Account for ballots & pack up supplies... Deliver the voted ballots & supplies to a central collection point.'

c3.evidence: Both pay and hours are published on slocounty.ca.gov, the County of San Luis Obispo Clerk-Recorder's own official site.

c4.evidence: Publisher is the San Luis Obispo County Clerk-Recorder's elections office; the county's own site maintains a dedicated 'November 3, 2026, General Election' page with 'Apply to be a Precinct Worker' links and lists precinct-worker recruitment under its November 3, 2026 General Election & Voter FAQs, confirming current-cycle recruitment.

s1.note: Compensation stated as a county-published approximate range ($50–$150) tied to role and half-/full-day shift, plus $20 training bonus.

s2.note: Hours explicit: 6:00 A.M. arrival for setup; work through close and post-close ballot accounting/delivery (open-ended end).

s3.note: Application path explicit via county precinct worker application and county precinctworker@co.slo.ca.us / 805-781-4989 contact.

s4.note: Mileage beyond the stipend: not stated by the county — treated as not published.

s5.note: Range varies by role and half-/full-day shift; no fixed role-by-role table published — caveat noted.

s6.note: Eligibility stated: 18+, U.S. citizen, registered CA voter or lawful permanent resident.

s7.note: No fees or cost barriers identified.

notes: San Luis Obispo County, California precinct (poll) workers. Individual stipend approximately $50–$150 by role and shift length, plus $20 for training attendance. Long Election Day starting 6:00 A.M. with post-close ballot accounting and delivery. Note: the county's larger ~$600-per-precinct figure is the Adopt-A-Poll program paid to organizations, not individuals.
payout_value_note: Approximate stipend of $50–$150 by role and half-/full-day shift, plus $20 for attending training; max includes the training bonus.
numeric_basis: 6:00 A.M. arrival to ~8:00 P.M. poll close = 14 hours (840 minutes); closing, ballot accounting/packing, and delivery to the collection point extend the day further — reasonably up to ~17 hours (1020 minutes).
